mainTopic: רב's permission to pluck a בכור's hair, דבר שאין מתכוין, and plucking hair to see a מום.
overview: The amud opens with the end of רב's ruling: one may clear the hair at a בכור's slaughter spot, even on יום טוב. The גמרא tests this against רב's ban on pressing a cloth stopper into a barrel and answers that the stopper is a פסיק רישיה case. Because רב rules like רבי יהודה, the גמרא concludes that he does forbid דבר שאין מתכוין. He permits clearing the hair because plucking hair is not shearing, and on יום טוב it is done כלאחר יד. Feathers are different, since plucking is the normal way to remove them. The גמרא then asks whether רבי יוסי בן המשולם also forbids unintended results, given that he lets one cut the black tips of a פרה אדומה's hairs. After several attempts, it answers either that the פרה is rare or that the agreement between רב and רבי יוסי בן המשולם goes only one way. Next, ריש לקיש limits the plucking to the hand, reading the משנה as 'לקופיץ'. The גמרא proves twice that plucking hair to see a מום is allowed לכתחילה. Finally, a new משנה begins about hair that fell off a blemished בכור before slaughter, where עקביא בן מהללאל permits it.

steps.title: The end of רב's ruling: it is permitted
steps.stepSummary: The closing word of רב's ruling: clearing the hair at the slaughter spot is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: This one word finishes רב's ruling from just before this section. Clearing the hair so the knife can reach the slaughter spot is allowed, even on יום טוב. The גמרא is about to test this ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While clearing the hair, a person might pull some hairs out without meaning to. Pulling out hair is a forbidden מלאכה. By saying מותר, רב seems to permit a דבר שאינו מתכוין, an act whose forbidden result is not intended.

keyTerms.meaning: an act whose forbidden result is not intended

phrases.english: It is permitted.
phrases.notes: This is the last word of רב's ruling from just before; clearing the hair for the knife is allowed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב's ruling, which began just before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Clearing hair from the slaughter spot is permitted, even though hair may be plucked without intent.

steps.title: Challenge from רב's ruling on the barrel stopper
steps.stepSummary: רב himself forbids pressing a cloth stopper into a barrel on יום טוב, which suggests he forbids unintended forbidden results.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did רב really say this? But רב חייא בר אשי said in the name of רב: it is forbidden to press a cloth barrel stopper in tightly on יום טוב!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ruling of מותר by quoting a different ruling of רב that seems stricter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the cloth stopper is pushed in, liquid gets squeezed out of it, even though the person does not want that. רב forbids it. So it looks like רב forbids a דבר שאינו מתכוין, and then he should also forbid clearing hair.

keyTerms.meaning: Did רב really say this? (a challenge formula)
a cloth stopper of a barrel

phrases.english: And did Rav really say this?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא אָמַר רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָשֵׁי מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב:
phrases.english: But didn't Rav Ḥiyya bar Ashi say in the name of Rav:
The cloth stopper of a barrel,
phrases.notes: Pushing the cloth in tightly squeezes liquid out of it, and squeezing is forbidden on יום טוב.

phrases.english: it is forbidden to press it in tightly on a Festival!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אָמַר רַב הָכִי? וְהָא אָמַר רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָשֵׁי מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the ruling in Step 1 using another ruling of רב.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's permission to clear the hair at the slaughter spot.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב forbids an unintended squeeze with the stopper, so he should also forbid unintended plucking of hair.

steps.title: The stopper is a פסיק רישיה case
steps.stepSummary: With the stopper, squeezing is unavoidable, and in such a case even רבי שמעון forbids it.
steps.simpleTranslation: In that case, even רבי שמעון agrees, as אביי and רבא both said: רבי שמעון agrees in a case of 'cut off its head and will it not die?'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the stopper case is different, because liquid will definitely be squeezed out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון normally permits an unintended forbidden result. He agrees that it is forbidden when the result is certain, which is called פסיק רישיה. Squeezing the stopper is certain, so forbidding it does not show that רב is strict about ordinary unintended acts. Pulling out hair is not certain.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Cut off its head and will it not die?': the forbidden result is certain to happen

steps.whatToRemember: An unintended forbidden result is permitted according to רבי שמעון. If the result is certain (פסיק רישיה), even רבי שמעון forbids it.
steps.confusionAlert: פסיק רישיה does not mean the person intends the result. It means the result is guaranteed, even though he does not want it.
steps.whyThisMatters: פסיק רישיה is a basic rule across הלכות שבת and יום טוב.

phrases.english: In that case, even Rabbi Shimon agrees,
as Abaye and Rava both say:
Rabbi Shimon agrees
in a case of 'cut off its head and will it not die?'
phrases.notes: It's a picture: if you chop off a chicken's head, of course it dies. The result is guaranteed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 2 by showing that the two cases are different.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases: a certain result versus an uncertain one.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The stopper ruling shows that רב forbids every unintended forbidden result.
steps.terutzMaskana: The stopper is forbidden only because of פסיק רישיה. רב can still follow רבי שמעון for ordinary unintended acts like clearing hair.

steps.title: Challenge: רב rules like רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: Two reports say רב rules like רבי יהודה, who forbids unintended forbidden results. That contradicts רב permitting the hair-clearing.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רב חייא בר אשי said in the name of רב that the הלכה follows רבי יהודה, and רב חנן בר אמי said in the name of שמואל that the הלכה follows רבי שמעון. And רב חייא בר אבין teaches it without naming the reporters: רב says the הלכה follows רבי יהודה, and שמואל says the הלכה follows רבי שמעון!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new challenge. רב rules like רבי יהודה, the strict view, so how can he permit clearing hair? The next step answers this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The last answer assumed that רב follows רבי שמעון for ordinary unintended acts. Now the גמרא brings two reports, one with named reporters and one without, both saying that רב rules like רבי יהודה. If so, רב should forbid the hair-clearing.

keyTerms.meaning: without naming the men who passed it on

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא אָמַר רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָשֵׁי אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: But didn't Rav Ḥiyya bar Ashi say that Rav said:
The halakha follows Rabbi Yehuda,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַב חָנָן בַּר אַמֵּי אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: and Rav Ḥanan bar Ami said that Shmuel said:
The halakha follows Rabbi Shimon.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָבִין מַתְנֵי בְּלָא גַּבְרֵי:
phrases.english: And Rav Ḥiyya bar Avin teaches it without the men:
phrases.notes: He gives the same rulings but leaves out the names of the people who passed them on.

phrases.english: Rav says the halakha follows Rabbi Yehuda,
and Shmuel says the halakha follows Rabbi Shimon!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא אָמַר רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָשֵׁי אָמַר רַב: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the assumption behind Step 3, that רב agrees with רבי שמעון on ordinary unintended acts.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רב permits ordinary unintended forbidden results, and so permits clearing the hair.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two separate reports say that רב rules like רבי יהודה, who forbids unintended forbidden results. That contradicts his permitting the hair-clearing.

steps.title: רב forbids unintended results, but plucking is not shearing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the contradiction by saying רב does forbid דבר שאין מתכוין, but plucking hair is not the forbidden act of shearing (גוזז). On יום טוב it is permitted because it is uprooting done in an unusual way (כלאחר יד).
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, really רב holds that an unintended forbidden result is forbidden. But plucking is not shearing. And the reason he permits it on יום טוב is that it is uprooting something from where it grows, done in an unusual way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops its earlier approach and gives a new answer to the contradiction from Step 4. רב forbids unintended results, but here there is no forbidden shearing at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 4 asked how רב can follow רבי יהודה and still permit clearing the hair. The answer: plucking is not גוזז, so a בכור's hair can be plucked without breaking the ban on shearing a בכור. The יום טוב concern (uprooting something from where it grows) is removed because it is done כלאחר יד, in an unusual manner.

keyTerms.meaning: An act that brings a forbidden result the person did not intend
Shearing; forbidden on a בכור and a labor on שבת
Uprooting something from the place where it grows
In an unusual or backhanded way, which is not a full Torah violation

steps.confusionAlert: Two separate problems are being solved here. The ban on shearing a בכור is solved by 'plucking is not shearing.' The יום טוב problem is solved by 'it is done in an unusual way.'

phrases.english: Rather, really Rav holds:
an unintended act is forbidden,
and plucking is not the same as shearing,
and on Yom Tov, this is the reason he permits it:
phrases.notes: This is about clearing the hair at the slaughter spot on יום טוב, when animals are slaughtered for food.

phrases.english: because it counts as uprooting something from where it grows
in an unusual way.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction from Step 4 by reframing why רב permits the act.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the act: plucking is not shearing, and on יום טוב it is done in an unusual manner.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב permits clearing the hair because he holds unintended results are allowed.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב forbids unintended results, but plucking is not גוזז, and on יום טוב it is כלאחר יד.

steps.title: A teaching shows plucking a feather counts as shearing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the claim that plucking is not shearing, using a ברייתא where plucking a feather on שבת is a separate חטאת, and ריש לקיש explains it is because of shearing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is plucking really not shearing? But a ברייתא teaches: one who plucks a feather, snips it, and strips it owes three חטאות. And ריש לקיש said: plucking is liable as shearing, snipping is liable as cutting, stripping is liable as smoothing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the new answer from Step 5 by bringing a ברייתא that seems to treat plucking as shearing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 depends on plucking not being גוזז. But ריש לקיש explains that plucking a feather makes one liable for the labor of shearing on שבת. So plucking does seem to be a kind of shearing.

keyTerms.meaning: A sin offering brought for an accidental transgression
A wing; here a large wing feather
Cutting to size, a שבת labor

phrases.english: And is plucking not the same as shearing?
But isn't it taught in a baraita:
One who plucks a wing feather,
and snips it, and strips it,
phrases.notes: Stripping means pulling off the soft threads along the sides of the feather.

phrases.english: is obligated to bring three sin offerings.
And Reish Lakish said:
Plucking: liable because of shearing,
snipping: liable because of cutting,
stripping: liable because of smoothing!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the key assumption of Step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in Step 5 that plucking is not shearing.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: ריש לקיש says plucking a feather is liable as גוזז, so plucking is a form of shearing.

steps.title: Feathers are different because plucking is their normal method
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that a feather is different: plucking is the normal way to remove feathers, so there it counts as shearing. With hair it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: A wing feather is different, because that is its normal way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends Step 5 by showing the ברייתא is about a special case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Feathers are normally removed by plucking, so for feathers plucking is the regular form of shearing. Hair is normally cut, not plucked, so plucking hair is not shearing. The answer in Step 5 stands.
steps.whatToRemember: רב forbids unintended results, but he holds plucking hair is not shearing, unlike plucking feathers, which is their normal method.

phrases.english: A wing feather is different,
because that is its normal way.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 6.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Plucking is always a form of shearing.
steps.terutzMaskana: Plucking counts as shearing only where it is the normal method, as with feathers.

steps.title: So רבי יוסי בן המשולם must agree with רב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא draws an inference: since רב follows רבי יוסי בן המשולם, then רבי יוסי בן המשולם must hold like רב, that דבר שאין מתכוין is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: And since רב holds like רבי יוסי בן המשולם, it follows that רבי יוסי בן המשולם holds like רב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a conclusion from what it just said. This sets up the next question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב's ruling on the hair follows רבי יוסי בן המשולם. Since we now say רב forbids unintended results and permits only because plucking is not shearing, רבי יוסי בן המשולם must have the same reasoning.

phrases.aramaic: וּמִדְּרַב סָבַר כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן הַמְשׁוּלָּם,
phrases.english: And since Rav holds like Rabbi Yosei ben HaMeshullam,

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן הַמְשׁוּלָּם סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַב,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei ben HaMeshullam holds like Rav.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִדְּרַב סָבַר כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן הַמְשׁוּלָּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the conclusion about רב to רבי יוסי בן המשולם.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוסי בן המשולם holds that דבר שאין מתכוין is forbidden, like רב.

steps.title: רבי יוסי בן המשולם lets one cut black hair-tips with scissors
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions the inference: a ברייתא shows רבי יוסי בן המשולם allows cutting black tips of two hairs with scissors without worry, which seems to show he permits unintended results.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does רבי יוסי בן המשולם really hold that an unintended act is forbidden? But a ברייתא teaches: two hairs whose roots are red and whose tops are black, רבי יוסי בן המשולם says: one cuts them with scissors and need not worry.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the inference of Step 8 using a ברייתא about a פרה אדומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Cutting the hair with scissors is real shearing of a holy animal, yet רבי יוסי בן המשולם says there is no worry. This seems to be because the person only wants to make the cow fit, not to shear it. That looks like permitting דבר שאין מתכוין, the opposite of Step 8.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it taught in a ברייתא; introduces a challenge from a source

phrases.english: And does Rabbi Yosei ben HaMeshullam hold
that an unintended act is forbidden?
But isn't it taught: two hairs,
phrases.notes: This is about a פרה אדומה, which becomes unfit if it has two black hairs.

phrases.english: whose roots are red and whose tops are black,
Rabbi Yosei ben HaMeshullam says:
One cuts them with scissors, and need not worry.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְסָבַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן הַמְשׁוּלָּם דָּבָר שֶׁאֵין מִתְכַּוֵּין אָסוּר? וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the inference made in Step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The inference that רבי יוסי בן המשולם forbids דבר שאין מתכוין.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: He permits real shearing of a holy animal with scissors because the person only means to make it fit, which suggests he permits unintended results.

steps.title: A cow is not an animal that gets sheared
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers Step 9: cutting the פרה's hairs is allowed because cows are not included in the ban on shearing.
steps.simpleTranslation: The red cow is different, because it is not an animal that gets sheared.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its first answer to the question from Step 9. The פרה אדומה is a cow, and the ban on shearing holy animals is only for wool animals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a cow is not covered by the ban on shearing, then cutting its hairs is not forbidden at all. So רבי יוסי בן המשולם's ruling here has nothing to do with דבר שאין מתכוין. His agreement with רב can still stand.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal that gets sheared (has wool)
The red cow, used for purifying people from טומאת מת

phrases.english: The red cow is different,
phrases.notes: This is the פרה אדומה from the ברייתא in Step 9, whose hair tips were cut with scissors.

phrases.english: for it is not an animal subject to shearing.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁאנֵי פָּרָה, דְּלָאו בַּת גִּיזָּה הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 9
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case: the subject is outside the prohibition
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Cutting the פרה's hair shows that רבי יוסי בן המשולם permits דבר שאין מתכוין
steps.terutzMaskana: Cows are not covered by the shearing ban, so there was never a prohibition to begin with

steps.title: A ברייתא says the shearing ban covers cattle too
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from the פסוק that the ban on shearing a בכור also applies to an ox, so a cow is included.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a ברייתא teaches: 'Do not work with the firstborn of your ox, and do not shear the firstborn of your flock.' From this I only know that an ox is forbidden for work and a sheep is forbidden for shearing. How do we know that each rule also applies to the other animal? The פסוק says 'Do not work... and do not shear.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the answer of Step 10. It brings a ברייתא showing that the shearing ban also applies to cattle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא reads the two halves of the פסוק as linked, so each rule covers both animals. That means an ox, or a cow, is included in the ban on shearing. So the claim that a cow is 'not an animal that gets sheared' does not work.

keyTerms.meaning: But it was taught in a ברייתא (opens a challenge)
A firstborn animal, which is holy

phrases.english: But it was taught in a ברייתא:
"You shall not work with the firstborn of your ox,
and you shall not shear the firstborn of your flock."
I would only know an ox regarding work
and a sheep regarding shearing.

phrases.aramaic: מִנַּיִן לִיתֵּן אֶת הָאָמוּר שֶׁל זֶה בָּזֶה
phrases.english: From where do we know to apply what was said of this one to that one,
and what was said of that one to this one?
The verse states: "You shall not work... and you shall not shear"!
phrases.notes: The extra word 'and' ties the two halves together, so both rules apply to both animals.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of Step 10
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that a cow is not subject to the shearing ban
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא applies the shearing ban to an ox, so a cow is included

steps.title: The פרה is holy only for Temple upkeep
steps.stepSummary: New answer: the פרה אדומה has the holiness of קדשי בדק הבית, and the shearing ban is not stated for that kind of holiness.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the red cow is different, because it has the holiness of items set aside for the upkeep of the בית המקדש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops its first answer and tries a new one. The פרה is not a קרבן on the מזבח; it belongs to the בית המקדש's upkeep fund.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban on shearing in the פסוק is about animals holy for the מזבח, like a בכור. The פרה אדומה has a different, lighter kind of holiness, so that ban would not apply to it.

keyTerms.meaning: Things made holy for the upkeep of the בית המקדש
Things made holy to be offered on the מזבח

phrases.english: Rather, the red cow is different,
for it has the holiness of Temple-upkeep property.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, שָׁאנֵי פָּרָה, דְּקׇדְשֵׁי בֶּדֶק הַבַּיִת הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the answer that Step 11 knocked down
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פרה is like any holy animal and may not be sheared
steps.terutzMaskana: Its holiness is for Temple upkeep, which the shearing ban does not cover

steps.title: רבי אלעזר says Temple-upkeep animals may not be sheared either
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר rules that קדשי בדק הבית are also forbidden for shearing and work.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רבי אלעזר said: things set aside for Temple upkeep are forbidden for shearing and for work!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer of Step 12 by quoting רבי אלעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי אלעזר forbids shearing even קדשי בדק הבית, then calling the פרה 'Temple-upkeep holy' does not explain why cutting its hair is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't he say? (opens a challenge)

phrases.english: But didn't רבי אלעזר say:
Temple-upkeep holy property
is forbidden for shearing and work!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks Step 12
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that קדשי בדק הבית may be sheared
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי אלעזר explicitly forbids shearing them

steps.title: That ban is only rabbinic
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר's ban on shearing קדשי בדק הבית comes from the רבנן, not from the תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is only a rabbinic ban.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers Step 13 with one word: רבי אלעזר's ban is מדרבנן. By the תורה itself, the פרה is still not covered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This keeps Step 12 alive. By the תורה, קדשי בדק הבית may be sheared. Only the רבנן added a ban.

keyTerms.meaning: A protective ban made by the Sages

phrases.english: By rabbinic law.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 13
steps.terutzResolutionType: Lowering the level of the prohibition
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אלעזר's ban is from the תורה

steps.title: A rabbinic ban is still a ban
steps.stepSummary: Even a rabbinic ban should stop a person from cutting the hairs, so why does the ברייתא say 'he need not worry'?
steps.simpleTranslation: But there is still a rabbinic prohibition!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on Step 14. Even if the ban is only from the רבנן, it is still forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא in Step 9 said a person may cut the hairs and not worry at all. A rabbinic ban would still be a reason to worry, so Step 14 does not solve the problem.

keyTerms.meaning: He need not worry (the wording of the ברייתא in Step 9)

phrases.english: But there is still a rabbinic prohibition!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks Step 14
steps.kashyaTarget: Answering the problem by calling the ban rabbinic
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A rabbinic ban still forbids the act, but the ברייתא allows it with no worry

steps.title: The פרה is rare, so the רבנן never banned it
steps.stepSummary: The פרה אדומה is uncommon, so the rabbinic ban on shearing Temple-upkeep animals was never applied to it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the red cow is different, because it is uncommon.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new answer. A פרה אדומה hardly ever happens, and the רבנן did not make their ban for rare cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By the תורה, Temple-upkeep animals may be sheared (Step 14). The rabbinic ban was made for common cases, and a פרה אדומה is very rare. So there is no ban at all on its hair, and רבי יוסי בן המשולם's ruling says nothing about דבר שאין מתכוין.

keyTerms.meaning: They (the Sages) did not make a ban

phrases.english: Rather, the red cow is different,
because it is uncommon.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 15 by limiting the rabbinic ban
steps.terutzResolutionType: The rabbinic ban does not reach rare cases
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The rabbinic ban covers the פרה too
steps.terutzMaskana: The רבנן did not ban rare cases, so the פרה's hair may be cut

steps.title: Why not redeem it, shear it, and make it holy again?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: instead of being lenient, why not redeem the פרה, shear it as an ordinary animal, and then make it holy again?
steps.simpleTranslation: But let him redeem it and make it ordinary, shear it, and then make it holy again!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the answer of Step 16. Even for a rare case, there is a simple way to avoid any problem, so why allow cutting the hair while it is holy?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the owner can easily take the holiness off, shear the animal, and put the holiness back, there would be no need for any leniency. That makes the leniency hard to understand.

keyTerms.meaning: To redeem, to move the holiness onto money

phrases.english: But let him redeem it and bring it out to ordinary status,
and shear it, and then make it holy again!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for the leniency of Step 16
steps.kashyaTarget: Allowing the hair to be cut while the פרה is still holy
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: There is an easy legal way to avoid the issue, so why permit it?

steps.title: The פרה is too expensive to redeem
steps.stepSummary: A פרה אדומה is worth a fortune, so redeeming it is not practical.
steps.simpleTranslation: Its price is very high.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers Step 17. To redeem the פרה you would have to pay its full value, and a פרה אדומה costs a huge amount.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Redeeming means giving money equal to the animal's worth. For such a valuable animal, we cannot expect the owner to do that just to cut some hairs.

phrases.english: Its value is expensive.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 17
steps.terutzMaskana: Redeeming at full value is too costly

steps.title: Use שמואל's rule: redeem it for a פרוטה
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that holy property worth a מנה, if redeemed for a פרוטה, is redeemed. So the cost should not be a problem.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let him do as שמואל says, for שמואל said: holy property worth a מנה that someone redeemed onto something worth a פרוטה is redeemed!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges Step 18 by quoting שמואל. If a cheap redemption works, the high price does not matter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל holds that redeeming for far less than the real value still works. Then the owner could redeem the פרה for a פרוטה, shear it, and make it holy again for almost no money.

phrases.english: But let him do with it as שמואל says,
for שמואל said:
Holy property worth a מנה
that one redeemed onto something worth a פרוטה
is redeemed!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks Step 18
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the high value prevents redemption
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שמואל allows redemption for a tiny amount, so cost is not an issue

steps.title: שמואל's rule works only after the fact
steps.stepSummary: שמואל only said the cheap redemption works once it is done. He never said one may do it from the start.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can say that שמואל said it works if he already redeemed it. Did he say one may do so from the start?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers Step 19. שמואל's rule is בדיעבד, so we cannot tell someone to plan a cheap redemption. The answer of Step 16 (the פרה is rare) stands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a difference between 'it works once done' and 'you are allowed to do it.' Since one may not plan a cheap redemption, redeeming is not a real option, and the leniency for the rare פרה makes sense.

keyTerms.meaning: From the start, as a plan

steps.whatToRemember: The first answer that holds is that the פרה אדומה is rare, so the rabbinic ban on shearing Temple-upkeep animals does not apply to it. That is why its hair may be cut, without any proof about דבר שאין מתכוין.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up 'it works' with 'it is allowed.' שמואל says a cheap redemption works after the fact, not that one may plan to do it.

phrases.english: Granted, שמואל said it works if he already redeemed it,
but did he say it may be done from the start?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימוֹר דְּאָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל שֶׁחִילְּלוֹ, לְכִתְחִלָּה מִי אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 19 and closes the line of answers
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing after the fact from planning ahead
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל allows a cheap redemption even as a plan
steps.terutzMaskana: It works only after the fact, so one cannot plan it

steps.title: The agreement goes only one way
steps.stepSummary: A different answer to Step 9: רב agrees with רבי יוסי בן המשולם, but רבי יוסי בן המשולם does not have to agree with רב about דבר שאין מתכוין.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say instead: רב holds like רבי יוסי בן המשולם, but רבי יוסי בן המשולם does not hold like רב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a completely different answer to Step 9. It rejects the reasoning of Step 8 instead of explaining away the פרה ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 8 reasoned: רב follows רבי יוסי בן המשולם, so רבי יוסי בן המשולם must also forbid דבר שאין מתכוין like רב. Here the גמרא says that does not follow. רב borrowed one ruling from him, but on דבר שאין מתכוין they can disagree, so the פרה ruling is no problem.

keyTerms.meaning: If you want, say (gives another answer)
An unintended result of a permitted act

steps.whatToRemember: There are two answers to Step 9. Either the פרה is a rare case the רבנן did not ban, or רבי יוסי בן המשולם never held like רב about דבר שאין מתכוין in the first place.
steps.whyThisMatters: It teaches that when one חכם follows another on a single ruling, that does not mean they agree on everything.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:

phrases.aramaic: רַב סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן הַמְשׁוּלָּם,
phrases.english: רב holds like רבי יוסי בן המשולם,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן הַמְשׁוּלָּם לָא סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַב.
phrases.english: but רבי יוסי בן המשולם does not hold like רב.
phrases.notes: He means on the question of דבר שאין מתכוין, which is what Step 8 tried to pin on him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: רַב סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן הַמְשׁוּלָּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, separate answer to the קשיא of Step 9
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since רב follows רבי יוסי בן המשולם, the two must agree on דבר שאין מתכוין
steps.terutzMaskana: The agreement is one-way; רבי יוסי בן המשולם may permit דבר שאין מתכוין

steps.title: The משנה lets the slaughterer pluck hair
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: the person slaughtering a בכור may pluck hair from the neck, as long as he does not move it from its place.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he plucks the hair, as long as he does not move it from its place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה so it can discuss it. This is a setup line for ריש לקיש's statement that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Shearing a בכור is forbidden. The משנה allows someone slaughtering it to pull out some hair to clear room for the knife, but the hair must stay where it is and not be taken away.

keyTerms.meaning: A firstborn animal, which is holy and may not be sheared
As long as, on condition that

phrases.english: And he plucks the hair,
phrases.notes: This is someone slaughtering a בכור and clearing space on the neck for his knife.

phrases.english: provided that he does not move it from its place.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתוֹלֵשׁ אֶת הַשֵּׂעָר, וּבִלְבַד שֶׁלֹּא יְזִיזֶנּוּ מִמְּקוֹמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the discussion of רבי יוסי בן המשולם and דבר שאין מתכוין to the next words of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A slaughterer may pluck hair from a בכור's neck, as long as he leaves it in place.

steps.title: Only by hand, not with a tool
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש, as quoted by רב אשי, says the משנה allows plucking only by hand. Using a tool is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said in the name of ריש לקיש: They only taught this when he plucks by hand. With a tool, it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש narrows the משנה's permission: plucking by hand is fine, but plucking with a tool is not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Using a tool on the hair looks like shearing, which is forbidden for a בכור. Plucking by hand does not look like shearing, so only that is allowed.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ:
phrases.english: Rav Ashi said that Reish Lakish said:
They taught this only by hand,
but with a tool, it is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the permission given in the משנה quoted in Step 22.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Plucking a בכור's hair is allowed by hand only, not with a tool.

steps.title: But the משנה mentions a cleaver
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges ריש לקיש: the משנה says he clears space 'with a cleaver', which is a tool.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the משנה teaches: He clears space with a cleaver on this side and that side!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks ריש לקיש using the משנה's own words, which mention a tool.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש said tools are forbidden. The משנה says the slaughterer makes room 'בקופיץ', with a cleaver. That sounds like the משנה allows a tool.

keyTerms.meaning: From here and from there, on both sides

phrases.english: But isn't it taught:
He clears space with a cleaver from here and from there!
phrases.notes: This is the line of the משנה just before 'and he plucks the hair'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges ריש לקיש from Step 23 using the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's rule that plucking with a tool is forbidden.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה plainly says the space is cleared 'with a cleaver', a tool.

steps.title: Read it as 'for a cleaver'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers by reading the משנה as 'לקופיץ', clearing space for the cleaver, not with it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Teach it as: 'for a cleaver'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by changing one letter in the משנה: he clears space by hand to make room for the cleaver.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Reading 'לקופיץ' instead of 'בקופיץ' means the cleaver is the knife used to slaughter, not the tool used on the hair. So ריש לקיש's rule stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Teach it as, read it as

phrases.english: Teach: 'for a cleaver'.
phrases.notes: Read 'ל' instead of 'ב'. He clears room by hand so the cleaver can cut.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 24.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the wording of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה allows clearing the hair with a cleaver.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה means clearing hair by hand for the cleaver. Plucking with a tool stays forbidden.
steps.whatToRemember: According to ריש לקיש, hair may be plucked from a בכור only by hand. The משנה is read 'לקופיץ', for the cleaver.

steps.title: Plucking hair to see a blemish
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: likewise, one may pluck hair to see a מום.
steps.simpleTranslation: And likewise, he plucks the hair to see a blemish.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next part of the משנה. This sets up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בכור may be slaughtered outside the מקדש only if it has a מום. Sometimes hair hides the מום, so the משנה allows pulling the hair out to show it.

keyTerms.meaning: A blemish, which allows a בכור to be slaughtered and eaten outside the מקדש

phrases.english: And likewise, he plucks the hair
to see a blemish.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵן תּוֹלֵשׁ אֶת הַשֵּׂעָר לִרְאוֹת מוּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next ruling of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may pluck hair from a בכור to see a מום.

steps.title: Allowed from the start or only after the fact?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether plucking hair to see a מום is allowed לכתחילה, or only accepted דיעבד.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: Is it allowed from the start, or only after it was done?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a real question: what level of permission does the משנה give for plucking hair to see a מום?
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'And likewise he plucks' could mean you may do it from the start. It could also mean that if he already did it, it is not a problem. The גמרא wants to know which one.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked among them
After the fact, once it was already done

phrases.english: A question was raised before them:
Is it from the start, or after the fact?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the ruling of the משנה quoted in Step 26.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether plucking hair to see a מום is allowed לכתחילה or only דיעבד.

steps.title: Proof from wool stuck in the ear
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה brings a ברייתא: if wool is tangled in the ear, רבי יוסי בן המשולם says one plucks it and shows the מום.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said: Come and hear: Wool tangled in the ear: רבי יוסי בן המשולם says, he plucks it and shows the blemish.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה brings a ברייתא to answer the question of Step 27.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי בן המשולם (the same תנא discussed earlier) tells you what to do: pluck the wool and show the מום. That sounds like an instruction from the start, not just accepting it afterward.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear, introducing a proof

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said: Come and hear,
Wool that is tangled in the ear,
phrases.notes: The tangled wool is hiding a מום in the בכור's ear.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei ben HaMeshullam says:
He plucks it and shows its blemish.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא to answer the question of Step 27.
steps.raayaObject: That plucking hair to see a מום is allowed לכתחילה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא quoting רבי יוסי בן המשולם about wool tangled in the ear.

steps.title: So it is allowed from the start
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes from the ברייתא that plucking to see a מום is allowed לכתחילה, and agrees.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn from this: from the start. Yes, learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts רבי ירמיה's proof: plucking hair to see a מום is allowed לכתחילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא tells a person to pluck and show the מום, so it is an instruction from the start. The גמרא agrees with the proof.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from it, conclude from it

phrases.english: Conclude from it: from the start,
Indeed, conclude from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the ברייתא in Step 28.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Plucking hair from a בכור to see a מום is allowed לכתחילה.

steps.title: רב מרי: our משנה teaches it too
steps.stepSummary: רב מרי says the same conclusion can be learned from the משנה itself, from the words 'and likewise one plucks the hair to see the place of a מום'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מרי said: We also learned this in our משנה: And likewise, one who plucks the hair to see the place of a blemish.
steps.whatsHappening: רב מרי brings a second proof, this time from the משנה itself. He quotes the line he will analyze in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב מרי points to the word 'וכן', 'and likewise'. He will show that this word only makes sense if it means plucking is allowed לכתחילה.

keyTerms.meaning: We too learned this (in our משנה)

phrases.english: Rav Mari said:
We too have learned it:
And likewise, one who plucks the hair
to see the place of a blemish.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second proof for the conclusion of Step 29.
steps.raayaObject: That plucking to see a מום is allowed לכתחילה.

steps.title: What does 'likewise' compare to?
steps.stepSummary: רב מרי asks what the word 'וכן' in the משנה is comparing to.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is 'and likewise'?
steps.whatsHappening: רב מרי asks a question to set up his proof: 'likewise' is like which earlier rule?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier line of the משנה had two parts: 'he plucks the hair' and 'he may not move it'. 'Likewise' could point to either one, and the next steps check both.

phrases.english: What is 'and likewise'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the analysis of the word רב מרי quoted in Step 30.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which earlier rule in the משנה the word 'וכן' is comparing to.

steps.title: It cannot mean 'don't move the hair'
steps.stepSummary: If 'likewise' meant 'he may not move the hair', it would be obvious and not needed. If a slaughterer, whose act shows he isn't shearing, may not move it, then surely someone checking a מום may not.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it means 'he may not move it from its place': Now, if a slaughterer, whose slaughtering shows what he is doing, may not move it, is it even necessary to say this about seeing the place of a blemish?
steps.whatsHappening: רב מרי rules out the first possible meaning of 'וכן', because then the משנה would be teaching something obvious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a person is slaughtering, everyone can see he is not shearing, yet he still may not move the hair. Someone checking a מום shows no such clear sign, so of course he may not move it either. The משנה would not need to say something that obvious.

keyTerms.meaning: Now, if even..., (a 'how much more so' argument)
Shows clearly about him, makes it plain
Is it even necessary to say?

steps.confusionAlert: This step does not say moving the hair is allowed when checking a מום. It is forbidden there too. The point is only that the משנה would not need 'וכן' to teach that, because it is obvious.

phrases.english: If you say it means that he may not move it from its place,
phrases.notes: Some versions have the words in round brackets; the corrected wording uses the words in square brackets instead, so read 'שלא יזיזנו ממקומו'.

phrases.english: now, if one who slaughters,
whose slaughtering shows clearly about him,
phrases.notes: Everyone can see he is slaughtering, not shearing the animal for its wool.

phrases.english: may not move it,
is it even necessary to say this about seeing the place of a blemish?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests and rejects the first possible answer to the question of Step 31.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The reading that 'וכן' refers to the rule of not moving the hair.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It would make the משנה teach something obvious, through a 'how much more so' argument from the slaughterer.

steps.title: 'Likewise' means plucking is allowed from the start
steps.stepSummary: So 'וכן' must refer to plucking itself: just as the slaughterer may pluck, one may pluck to see a מום, and that is allowed לכתחילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, isn't it referring to plucking? Conclude from it: from the start. Yes, conclude from it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב מרי finishes his proof: 'וכן' compares to the permission to pluck, so plucking to see a מום is allowed לכתחילה. The גמרא agrees.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The slaughterer is allowed to pluck from the start. Since 'וכן' compares checking a מום to that, it is also allowed from the start. This confirms what was learned from the ברייתא in Step 29.
steps.whatToRemember: Plucking hair from a בכור to see a מום is allowed לכתחילה. This is proven twice: from רבי יוסי בן המשולם's ברייתא and from the word 'וכן' in the משנה.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how the גמרא can draw a ruling from one small word like 'וכן': once one meaning would be pointless, the other meaning must be right.

phrases.english: Rather, isn't it referring to the plucking?
Conclude from it: from the start,
Indeed, conclude from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting the first option in Step 32, adopts the remaining meaning of 'וכן' and concludes.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: 'וכן' compares to the permission to pluck, so plucking hair to see a מום is allowed לכתחילה.

steps.title: New משנה: hair that fell off a blemished firstborn
steps.stepSummary: The משנה describes hair that fell off a בכור בעל מום while it was alive, was put away, and then the animal was slaughtered. עקביא בן מהללאל rules that the hair is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: MISHNA: Hair of a blemished firstborn animal fell out, and the owner put it away in a wall niche. Afterward he slaughtered the animal. עקביא בן מהללאל permits the hair.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens with a case about hair that fell off a blemished בכור while it was still alive. עקביא בן מהללאל gives the first ruling: the hair may be used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once a blemished בכור is slaughtered, the hair still on its body may be used. The new question is about hair that fell out earlier, while the animal was alive. עקביא בן מהללאל treats that hair as permitted once the animal has been slaughtered.

keyTerms.meaning: A firstborn animal that has a blemish, so it cannot be brought as a קרבן
That fell out on its own
Here, a small niche or cubby in the wall used for storing things
A תנא who gives the first opinion in this משנה

steps.confusionAlert: עקביא בן מהללאל is not saying the hair may be used while the animal is still alive. The case he rules on is one where the animal was later slaughtered.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
The hair of a blemished firstborn animal that fell out,
and he placed it in a niche,
and afterward he slaughtered the animal —
עקביא בן מהללאל permits the hair,

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ שְׂעַר בְּכוֹר בַּעַל מוּם שֶׁנָּשַׁר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The previous discussion about plucking hair to check for a מום has ended. A new משנה opens a new topic: hair that fell off before slaughter.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to עקביא בן מהללאל, hair that fell off a בכור בעל מום while it was alive and was set aside may be used after the animal is slaughtered.
